articles.title: The strait may reopen, but global confidence may not return | Opinions | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Strait of Hormuz may reopen, but global confidence in the stability of trade routes remains uncertain. Donald Trump's claim that a deal to reopen the strait has been largely negotiated provides temporary calm, but the deeper issue is who controls access and sets the rules for commerce. This shift from disruption to governance raises concerns about predictability and security for international trade.  The implications extend beyond the Gulf region, impacting Asia and developing economies reliant on energy and shipping. While diplomacy may succeed in restoring temporary peace, it does not guarantee long-term stability.

articles.title: Ukrainian drone attacks hit multiple Russian targets, including refinery | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ukrainian drones have targeted multiple Russian regions, including the Saratov refinery and oil pumping stations in Kirov and Lazarevo. Governor Roman Busargin of Saratov reported damage to civilian infrastructure after overnight strikes.  The Ukrainian army confirmed these attacks while denying claims that they hit the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy requested additional air defense ammunition from allies, including a new Iris-T missile launcher from Germany.

articles.title: US Iran War China Chinese Missile Likely Downed US F-15 Fighter Jet In Iran: Report
articles.rephrased_article: A US F-15 fighter jet that crashed over Iran last month may have been downed by a China-made missile, according to new reports.  China may have also provided Iran with additional military support, including stealth aircraft technology and long-range radar systems. The incident is significant as it could be the first time in decades a US fighter jet has been brought down by enemy fire. US officials are still investigating how the jet was shot down, but the crash triggered a 36-hour search operation to locate the crew.  The incident may further strain relations between the US and China.

articles.title: From Social Media Star To Terror Suspect: Pakistan’s Shahzad Bhatti Under Indian Security Scanner | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Shahzad Bhatti, a Pakistani social-media influencer, is the subject of multiple Indian security probes alleging his involvement in a cross-border crime and terror network.  Indian investigators have arrested nine individuals suspected of planning attacks on religious sites and military facilities, with Bhatti claiming to be neither a gangster nor a mafia boss.  He has been linked to criminal figures in Pakistan and is accused of radicalizing unemployed youth for his online network, which Indian agencies are monitoring.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of cross-border crime and terror networks raise serious security concerns.

articles.title: Pakistan beaming rogue telecom signals to aid terror networks, penetrate jails in Jammu and Kashmir: Officials - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan is accused of violating international telecommunication norms by broadcasting superfluous cellular signals across the border into Jammu and Kashmir, aiming to provide a covert communication lifeline to terrorist groups.  The signals, particularly in the Jammu region, reach various jails where hardcore terrorists are incarcerated. Officials say that traditional jammers have been ineffective against these rogue signals, which utilize advanced technology like CDMA and YSMS. The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) has previously condemned such transmissions as forbidden, and security agencies are working to dismantle the network.

articles.title: Laos cave survivors help with plan to find last two missing men
articles.rephrased_article: Laos authorities are working with survivors of a recent cave rescue to locate the remaining two men trapped inside. The five rescued individuals, all local villagers who entered the cave seeking gold, provided information about the deeper sections of the cave system, which is being used to guide search efforts. Japanese and international divers are assisting in the operation, while authorities are also exploring ways to drain flood water from the tunnels.

articles.title: Hundreds arrested and dozens of police injured after Champions League riots in France
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of people were arrested and dozens of police officers injured in clashes between football fans and police following Paris Saint-Germain's (PSG) victory in the Champions League final. The violence disrupted public transportation services in Paris, with thousands of officers deployed to maintain order.  The interior minister stated that security forces would be "firm" in their response to prevent further unrest. Marine Le Pen, leader of the far-right party, criticized the events, stating that they are unique to France.

articles.title: Water, gas & power outages - Pakistan's Karachi hit by utility collapse as Eid turns into crisis - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Millions of residents in Karachi faced severe disruptions during Eid-ul-Adha due to widespread water shortages, gas outages and power cuts. Residents accused Sui Southern Gas Company and Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation of failing to provide promised services despite official assurances.  K-Electric also faced criticism for scheduled outages and intermittent power supply. Protests erupted in several areas as residents blocked roads and expressed frustration over the disruptions, impacting their ability to cook, bathe and preserve food during the religious festival.

articles.title: Watch: Russia's 'fire-and-forget' $500 Yolka drone hunter that fits in soldier's hand - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: New video footage shows Russian forces deploying the handheld "Yolka" drone interceptor system in combat. The compact, "fire-and-forget" weapon, designed to counter enemy drones, was first seen during Russia's Victory Day military parade in May 2025 and has since been used in September 2024.  The Yolka does not carry an explosive warhead but instead relies on direct kinetic impact to destroy or disable hostile drones.

articles.title: Ukraine receives new German IRIS-T air defence launcher amid continued Russian missile and drone attacks - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that the country received a new IRIS-T air defense launcher from Germany, further bolstering its defenses against Russian missile and drone attacks. This latest delivery follows previous transfers of IRIS-T systems, with Zelenskyy previously stating that two additional launchers were crucial to Ukraine's air defense network. The IRIS-T SLM, a German-made medium-range surface-to-air missile system developed by Diehl Defence, is designed to intercept various aerial threats.

articles.title: UK Sikh restaurateur Harman Singh calls for kirpan ban, says it is being used against unarmed civilians | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Harman Singh Kapoor, a UK-based Sikh restaurateur, has called for a ban on kirpans, citing the recent conviction of Vickrum Digwa for murdering a university student with a kirpan.  Zia Yusuf, a spokesperson for Reform UK, has stated his party's intention to abolish the legal exemption allowing Sikhs to carry kirpans if elected. The issue has sparked debate within and beyond the Sikh community, with supporters arguing that most kirpan carriers use them as religious symbols rather than weapons.

articles.title: How China and India view growing unrest in Myanmar
articles.rephrased_article: China has been working to maintain a close relationship with the Myanmar military junta while balancing its support for rebel groups. The Chinese Ambassador to Myanmar, Ma Jia, met with defense minister General Tin Aung San to discuss strengthening military cooperation and border security.  Despite diplomatic efforts, including a visit by foreign minister Wang Yi, China has conducted live fire drills near the border with Myanmar to deter rebels and safeguard its investments. Beijing is also using economic leverage, threatening to halt trade if the civil conflict escalates further. The situation in Myanmar poses a challenge for both China and India, which are concerned about instability and refugee inflows.

articles.title: Deepest incursion in 26 years: Israeli forces capture strategic Beaufort Castle in southern Lebanon | World News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Express's Global Desk provides authoritative coverage of international developments, focusing on US and Canadian immigration policies.  Led by Aniruddha Dhar, Nischai Vats, and Mashkoora Khan, the desk reports on student visas, work permits, permanent residency pathways, executive actions, court rulings, study permits, post-study work options, and regulatory updates affecting migrants and international students. The reporting adheres to The Indian Express's editorial standards, relying on official data and verified sources.

articles.title: One Piece flag in Mexico protests | One Piece pirate flag becomes symbol of resistance for Gen Z protesters in Mexico - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: Luffy's pirate flag from the anime One Piece has become a symbol of resistance for Gen Z protestors in Mexico, who are protesting against growing crime and corruption.  The iconic Jolly Roger, representing freedom and rebellion against authority, emerged during clashes with riot police in Mexico City where protesters tore down fences around the National Palace. The incident resulted in injuries to 100 police officers and 20 civilians. Pablo Vazquez, Mexico City’s public safety secretary, confirmed the injuries.

articles.title: One Piece flag in Mexico protests | One Piece pirate flag becomes symbol of resistance for Gen Z protesters in Mexico - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: Luffy’s pirate flag, a symbol of freedom and defiance from the anime One Piece, has emerged as a rallying cry for Gen Z protestors in Mexico City.  The iconic Jolly Roger, representing rebellion against authority, was seen during clashes with police who responded to protesters tearing down fences around the National Palace. The incident resulted in injuries to both police officers and civilians, prompting calls for justice from those inspired by Luffy’s quest for freedom in the anime.

articles.title: Italian PM Giorgia Meloni warns her staff that 2026 will be "much worse" than 2025 - The Tribune
articles.rephrased_article: Giorgia Meloni, the Italian Prime Minister, warned her staff that 2026 will be "much worse" than 2025 due to economic challenges and global uncertainties.  She acknowledged their hard work during the year and advised them to rest during the holidays. Antonio Tajani, the Italian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, confirmed a planned visit by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Italy in 2026, highlighting discussions on strengthening India-Italy relations and cooperation on issues like peace and trade.

articles.title: Trump on Iran promise to not attack neighbours | Iran’s ‘surrender’ to its neighbours is because it is being ‘beat to HELL’, says Donald Trump - Telegraph India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump claimed Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's statement on suspending attacks against neighboring countries was a result of US-Israeli aggression.  Trump asserted that Iran had apologized and surrendered to its Middle Eastern neighbors due to these attacks, calling it the first time Iran has ever lost to surrounding countries. Pezeshkian, in his televised address, rejected the US demand for unconditional surrender, apologizing for Iran's attacks on regional countries and promising to halt them.

articles.title: After Vietnam, Indonesia To Buy India's Brahmos Missile: What Makes It Special
articles.rephrased_article: India has signed a deal to export its BrahMos supersonic cruise missile to Vietnam, with an agreement in the final stages with Indonesia. The deal, worth approximately Rs 5,800 crore, includes coastal defense missile batteries, missiles, training and logistics support.  The agreements are seen as strategically significant for India as it seeks to increase its influence in the region amidst tensions with China.  These deals could potentially see several countries around the South China Sea operating the BrahMos missile system.

articles.title: How Pakistan's Social Media Star Shahzad Bhatti Became ISI's New Weapon
articles.rephrased_article: Shahzad Bhatti, a Pakistani social media influencer linked to the ISI, is at the center of a major crackdown by Indian security agencies.  Bhatti's network, which recruits vulnerable youth through social media, allegedly involves criminal activity, radicalization, and plans for attacks on police personnel and sensitive locations. The Delhi Police Special Cell arrested eight suspects connected to Bhatti's module, recovering weapons and explosives. Investigations also reveal links to the Tehreek-e-Taliban Hindustan and a network of violent crimes in Punjab, including the grenade attack on a YouTuber.  Bhatti faces multiple investigations and threats from rival gangs like the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, highlighting his complex role in India's security landscape.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Alleged ISI recruitment and radicalization of youth pose a serious security threat.

articles.title: Donald Trump's daughter visits Jaisalmer, security heightened - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tiffany Trump and her husband, Michael Boulos, arrived in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan on Sunday (May 31, 2026) for a private visit.  They were welcomed by local officials and security personnel before visiting key tourist attractions. The couple is scheduled to stay overnight and depart for Delhi on Monday (June 1, 2026). This visit has generated excitement among local tourism stakeholders.

articles.title: US-Iran war news, "Very Interesting": President Donald Trump Says Iran Has Agreed To No Nuclear Weapons, Iran nuclear programme
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump claims to have secured a guarantee from Iran that it will not develop nuclear weapons, but Iran demands the release of $12 billion in frozen assets before substantive talks on nuclear issues.  The US and Iran remain far apart on key priorities, with Trump hinting at renewed military action if an agreement is not reached. Despite a temporary ceasefire, flare-ups of armed conflict have continued, including a recent incident where Iran's Revolutionary Guards shot down a US drone. Diplomatic efforts continue as both sides seek to lift the blockades around the Strait of Hormuz and end the ongoing fighting in Lebanon.

articles.title: Operation Sindoor Fallout: Pakistan Signs $1.2m FARA Contract To Intensify Washington Lobbying | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan has signed a $1.2 million contract with the US firm Ervin Graves Strategy Group LLC to bolster its influence in Washington. The two-year agreement will see the firm lobby members of Congress and senior officials across various US executive departments, aiming to position Pakistan as a reliable partner in counterterrorism and regional stability while advancing its diplomatic, economic, and strategic interests. This lobbying surge follows a previous push after India’s Operation Sindoor, which aimed to protect Pakistan's standing with international bodies like the Financial Action Task Force.

articles.title: Meteor explodes over US with blast equivalent to 300 tonnes of TNT - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, releasing an energy equivalent to 300 tonnes of TNT. NASA's deputy news chief Jennifer Dooren stated that the event was not associated with any active meteor shower but was a natural object. The explosion caused loud booms that alarmed residents, echoing across the region.  This incident follows a similar event in Chelyabinsk, Russia, where a house-sized space rock exploded in 2013, causing significant damage and injuries.

articles.title: Fresh Israeli Air strikes And Evacuations Reported Across Southern Lebanon | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Nawaf Salam, Lebanon's prime minister, accused Israel of a "scorched-earth policy" in the south, following fresh Israeli air strikes and evacuation warnings.  Salam defended his government's engagement with Israel, citing US-brokered talks that aimed to find a ceasefire. The May 29 talks included military delegations from both sides, but no mention was made of the truce intended to halt fighting between Israel and Hezbollah.  The escalation resulted in reports of multiple attacks across southern Lebanon, including Israeli drone strikes on Lebanese soldiers, and Hezbollah retaliatory attacks targeting northern Israel. The conflict has resulted in over 3,371 civilian casualties since March 2nd, according to the Lebanese health ministry.

articles.title: Israel issues more displacement orders in Lebanon, seizes strategic castle | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has issued more displacement orders in southern Lebanon, forcing residents to move north of the Zahrani River as it expands its invasion. Israel captured Beaufort Castle, a strategic hill near Nabatieh, and crossed the Litani River for the first time since 2006.  The Israeli military claims this is a tactical victory, while Lebanon's Prime Minister condemns Israel's actions as a "scorched-earth policy" and accuses it of collective punishment against residents. Hezbollah continues to target Israeli forces with drones, causing casualties. Despite peace talks facilitated by the United States, both sides remain entrenched in their positions.

articles.title: Colombia votes in presidential election that could redefine relations with US
articles.rephrased_article: Colombia is holding a presidential election with the potential to reshape its foreign relations, particularly with the United States.  The outcome could determine how the country addresses drug trafficking and violence.  Gustavo Petro, the current president, has endorsed Iván Cepeda, while other candidates include Abelardo de la Espriella and Paloma Valencia.  De la Espriella and Valencia have pledged a military crackdown if elected, while Cepeda maintains his commitment to "total peace" negotiations. The election follows months of strained relations between Petro and Donald Trump, the former US president.

articles.title: Donald Trump's daughter visits Jaisalmer, security heightened - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tiffany Trump and her husband, Michael Boulos, arrived in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan on Sunday (May 31, 2026) for a private visit. The couple was welcomed by local officials and security personnel from various agencies. They are scheduled to explore tourist attractions like Sonar Fort and Gadisar Lake before departing for Delhi on Monday (June 1, 2026).  The visit has generated excitement among local tourism stakeholders.

articles.title: Security forces detain PoK national, local woman near LoC in Uri
articles.rephrased_article: Security forces in north Kashmir's Baramulla district detained a Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) resident, Zeeshan Ahmad Mir, and a woman from Uri, Iram Bano, near the Line of Control.  Mir, a resident of Muzaffarabad, was apprehended by the Army's 12 Grenadiers unit, along with Bano. Both are in custody for questioning regarding their cross-border movement. Separately, security forces apprehended a former Territorial Army personnel attempting to cross the LoC. Investigations are ongoing in both cases.

articles.title: FIA offloaded nearly 39,800 passengers in 2025 to curb human smuggling, official says - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) offloaded 39,786 passengers in 2025 under a risk-based system to curb irregular migration and human smuggling. The agency cited concerns about suspicious travel patterns, document verification, destination-country requirements, and established procedures as reasons for the decisions.  Nouman Siddiqui, Immigration Additional Director General, emphasized that offloading was primarily aimed at protecting lives and preventing exploitation by traffickers.  The FIA also reported a 75% reduction in deportations related to beggary and a 31% decrease in those due to forgery, while overall deportations fell 16% compared to the previous year. The agency is implementing reforms including pre-departure facilitation desks and a 24/7 helpline for passengers who believe they were wrongly offloaded.

articles.title: Trump tightens terms on Iran war deal, US media say | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump has proposed changes to a potential agreement to end the US-Israel war on Iran, according to US media reports.  The new terms involve strengthening certain points of the deal, including what to do with Iran's nuclear material. Trump is seeking assurances that Iran will never develop nuclear weapons and the reopening of the blockaded Strait of Hormuz. Iran has yet to respond to these changes, but officials say it could take several days for a response.

articles.title: Japan's defence minister denies militarism and criticises China's 'huge arsenal'
articles.rephrased_article: Shinjiro Koizumi, Japan's defense minister, refuted China's claims of Japan engaging in "new militarism," stating that it was China's vast arsenal and lack of transparency that posed a concern to the international community.  Koizumi argued that Japan was simply updating its defenses to meet new challenges and contribute to peace in the region while emphasizing transparency and dialogue with other countries. He also criticized China for increasing its military spending without sufficient transparency, highlighting the difference between China's actions and Japan's peaceful intentions.

articles.title: Rajnath, Australian Deputy PM to hold second India-Australia Defence Ministers’ Dialogue in New Delhi
articles.rephrased_article: Shri Rajnath Singh, India's Raksha Mantri, and Mr Richard Marles, Australia's Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister, will co-chair the second India-Australia Defence Ministers’ Dialogue in New Delhi on June 1, 2026. The meeting aims to review progress in bilateral defence cooperation and identify new avenues for collaboration, focusing on strengthening defence & security cooperation, enhancing military interoperability, industry collaboration, and regional & global security developments of mutual interest. This visit follows the inaugural dialogue held in Australia in October 2025 and reflects the growing momentum in the India-Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

articles.title: In outreach to Bangladesh PM, India hails his father's 1971 address - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: India commemorated the 45th death anniversary of former Bangladesh President Zia-ur-Rahman, recalling his historic radio broadcast from March 1971, where he declared Bangladesh's independence and urged resistance against the Pakistani army. The Indian High Commission in Dhaka praised Zia-ur-Rahman as a "brave son" of the nation, highlighting his role in inspiring the people to fight for liberation.  The broadcast is seen as a pivotal moment in the struggle for Bangladesh's independence.

articles.title: Disabled another ship trying to defy blockade to reach Iran: US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US military disabled a merchant vessel, the Lian Star, attempting to enter an Iranian port after it ignored warnings. The ship remains adrift in the Gulf of Oman.  President Donald Trump stated that any peace deal must adhere to his red lines regarding Iran's nuclear program and the US warned it is "more than capable" of resuming war with Iran. The Pentagon chief, Pete Hegseth, echoed this stance at a defense summit in Singapore. Meanwhile, the US state department announced the dismantling of an Iranian network that defrauded American technology companies to acquire military equipment for Iran's defense sector.

articles.title: SpaceX wins $4bn contract for US Golden Dome satellites - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX has been awarded a $4.16 billion contract by the US Space Force to build satellites for its Golden Dome defensive shield program. The space-based network, which integrates sensors, communication systems and AI processing, aims to provide comprehensive air defense by monitoring threats from orbit.  The project is part of a layered defense strategy that includes ground-based sensors and military aircraft. SpaceX is already involved in developing prototypes of space-based interceptors for the program and collaborating with the US Space Force on a classified military communications network using its Starshield platform.

articles.title: Raise defence spending or else, Hegseth tells NATO, Europe - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth criticized NATO members for failing to meet their defense spending goals, stating those who don't increase their contributions will face a shift in how the US does business.  He cited South Korea as an example of a country that has invested heavily in its own defense due to its geographical location and real threat environment. Hegseth also praised other countries like Australia, the Philippines, and Japan for increasing their defense spending, emphasizing the importance of shared responsibility within alliances.

articles.title: At summit, AI dangers dwarf nuclear concerns - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Lieutenant General Nauman Zakria, Commander of 1 Corps and Army Rocket Force Command of the Pakistan army, and Mirjana Spoljaric, president of the International Committee of the Red Cross, warned at a defense forum in Singapore that artificial intelligence could reduce reaction times to the point where humans make rash decisions. They expressed concerns about AI's potential for escalating conflict as it could create "fog" in the OODA loop and lead to extreme actions. General Onno Eichelsheim, chief of defence of the Netherlands, also noted the use of AI on the battlefield, highlighting its risks in escalation while acknowledging its inevitable deployment.

articles.title: AUKUS to develop unmanned undersea vehicles, Pentagon chief says - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US, Britain, and Australia are collaborating on a trilateral project to develop unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs) as part of their Aukus defense pact. The program, which will begin delivery in 2027, aims to enhance the nations' reconnaissance and strike capabilities, bolstering their anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare, mine countermeasures, electronic warfare, and contested littoral maneuver capabilities.  The project falls under Aukus's "Pillar Two" initiative focused on developing advanced defense technologies.

articles.title: These Ebola Researchers Are Stuck in US Due to Trump’s Funding Cuts | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: The National Institutes of Health (NIH), which funded the Centers for Research in Emerging Infectious Diseases (CREID) Network, abruptly cut funding last year, citing safety concerns and a lack of alignment with priorities. The network, established to study viruses that emerge from wildlife and spread to humans, was instrumental in developing diagnostics and genomic sequencing during past Ebola outbreaks.  The decision has left researchers unable to provide crucial support on the ground in the Democratic Republic of Congo where an ongoing Ebola outbreak is rapidly spreading. Andrew Nixon, a spokesperson for the Department of Health and Human Services, stated that NIH will continue funding the program but did not elaborate on future plans.

articles.title: US Treasury sanctions Iran's Hormuz strait authority
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has sanctioned the Persian Gulf Strait Authority, a body Iran established to manage the Strait of Hormuz. The Treasury Department stated that anyone cooperating with the authority may be supporting and receiving services from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. This action comes as Tehran seeks to control global maritime trade, particularly after closing the strait following the US-Israel war against Iran in February.

articles.title: China expels NYT reporter over interview with Taiwan president - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: China expelled Vivian Wang, a New York Times journalist, from the country in February. The expulsion is attributed to an interview conducted by Andrew Ross Sorkin of Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te with the New York Times.  The Chinese government has previously criticized Wang's reporting on sensitive topics such as censorship and the Covid pandemic.

articles.title: Iran-US News LIVE: ‘Close to a deal,’ says Trump on peace negotiations, seeks no nuclear weapons promise from Tehran | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump has requested changes to a proposed peace deal with Iran, sending the new framework back for consideration. The changes, according to reports, aim to strengthen certain points of the agreement, particularly regarding Iran's nuclear material and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. This move could prolong negotiations between the parties, potentially delaying a decision on ending the West Asia war.  The outcome of these discussions remains uncertain, with both sides far apart on key priorities.

articles.title: Indian-origin Disney manager Jugal Daterao gets 2.5-year jail term in Russia over drug case - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jugal Daterao, an Indian-origin manager at The Walt Disney Company, was sentenced to two and a half years in a Russian prison after being convicted of drug possession and smuggling.  Customs officials found THC-infused gummy candies in his luggage at Moscow's Sheremetyevo International Airport, leading to his arrest in January 2026. Daterao argued that the gummies were prescribed for brain surgery recovery but was found guilty under Russian drug laws.

articles.title: Israel captures strategic Lebanon castle after days of fighting despite ceasefire - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli troops captured the strategic Beaufort Castle in southern Lebanon, marking their deepest incursion into the country since 1982. The Israeli military claimed the operation was launched to dismantle Hezbollah infrastructure and eliminate threats to Israeli civilians.  The capture comes despite a ceasefire agreement and ongoing direct talks between Israel and Lebanon in Washington.  Hezbollah has not yet responded to the latest advance, but tensions remain high along the border.
